title: ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN
description: Learn how to modify a column's data type, size, or add a NOT NULL constraint using ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN.

data.text: SQL Server ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN
The ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN statement modifies an existing column of a table. You can change the data type, change the size, or add a NOT NULL constraint.

data.title: ALTER COLUMN Syntax
data.content: Changes the data type of an existing column.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE table_name
ALTER COLUMN column_name new_data_type(size);

data.text: The new data type must be compatible with the old one. If the column has data that cannot be converted, the statement will fail with a conversion error.

data.title: Change INT to VARCHAR
data.content: Demonstrates converting a column from INT to VARCHAR and back.

data.text: Converting VARCHAR back to INT fails if the column contains non-numeric data, resulting in a conversion error.
Change the Size of a Column
You can increase or decrease the size of a column. When decreasing, SQL Server checks existing data to ensure it fits within the new size.

data.title: Increase Column Size
data.content: Increases VARCHAR size from 10 to 50 characters.

data.title: Decrease Column Size Fails
data.content: Attempting to decrease VARCHAR size to 5 fails due to existing data.
data.code: ALTER TABLE t2 ALTER COLUMN c VARCHAR (5);

data.title: Error
data.text: SQL Server issues 'String or binary data would be truncated' when existing data exceeds the new column size.
To add a NOT NULL constraint to a nullable column, you must first update any NULL values to non-null values, then alter the column.

data.title: Add NOT NULL Constraint
data.content: Updates NULL values then adds NOT NULL constraint.

data.title: ALTER COLUMN Key Points
points: Use ALTER COLUMN to change a column's data type, size, or nullability.
The new data type must be compatible with existing data.
Increasing column size is always safe; decreasing may fail if data doesn't fit.
To add NOT NULL, first update NULL values, then alter the column.
Existing data is preserved during column modifications.
